title.en: What is HTML?
title.hi: HTML क्या है?

theory.en: HTML stands for Hypertext Markup Language and is known as the language of the Internet used to create web pages. An HTML document is a plain-text file saved with a .html or .htm extension. It is created and edited in text editors like Notepad and viewed in web browsers like Google Chrome.

learning_units.pedagogical_objective: Explain angled bracket notation (<...>), browser rendering directives, and case-insensitive execution.

title.en: HTML Tags and Case Insensitivity
title.hi: HTML टैग और केस असंवेदनशीलता

theory.en: HTML tags are coded commands enclosed within angled brackets (`<` and `>`) that tell the web browser how to display content on a web page. HTML tags are not case-sensitive, meaning tags written in lowercase (like `<html>`) and uppercase (like `<HTML>`) are treated identically by the browser.
theory.hi: HTML टैग कोडित कमांड होते हैं जो कोण-कोष्ठक (`<` और `>`) के भीतर लिखे जाते हैं। ये ब्राउज़र को बताते हैं कि सामग्री को कैसे प्रदर्शित किया जाए। HTML टैग केस सेंसिटिव (case-sensitive) नहीं होते हैं, अर्थात इन्हें लोअर-केस (`<html>`) और अपर-केस (`<HTML>`) दोनों में समान रूप से लिखा जा सकता है।

title.en: HTML Document Structure: html, head, and title
title.hi: HTML दस्तावेज़ संरचना: html, head और title

theory.en: An HTML document is organized into structured structural sections. The `<html>...</html>` tag is the root container that encloses all other tags. The `<head>...</head>` tag contains metadata and header information about the document. Placed inside the `<head>` section, the `<title>...</title>` tag specifies the web page title displayed on the browser window's title bar or tab.
theory.hi: HTML दस्तावेज़ की एक निश्चित संरचना होती है: 1. `<html>...</html>`—यह रूट (root) सेक्शन है जिसके अंदर अन्य सभी टैग लिखे जाते हैं; 2. `<head>...</head>`—इसमें दस्तावेज़ के बारे में जानकारी (metadata) होती है; 3. `<title>...</title>`—यह `<head>` सेक्शन के अंदर लिखा जाता है और इसका टेक्स्ट ब्राउज़र के टाइटल बार या टैब में दिखाई देता है।

title.en: The BODY Tag: bgcolor and background

theory.en: The `<body>...</body>` tag contains all the visible content rendered on a web page, including text, images, tables, and hyperlinks. The `bgcolor` attribute defines the solid background color of the web page (e.g., `<BODY bgcolor="yellow">`). The `background` attribute sets a background image by supplying its file path (e.g., `<BODY background="flower.jpg">`), tiling the image across the page canvas.

title.en: BODY Attributes: text, leftmargin, and topmargin
title.hi: BODY ऐट्रिब्यूट: text, leftmargin और topmargin

theory.en: The `<body>` tag controls global viewport spacing and default typography color: `text` defines the global color of all body copy (e.g., `<BODY text="blue">`). `leftmargin` defines the distance in pixels between the left edge of the browser window and the page content (e.g., `<BODY leftmargin="100px">`). `topmargin` defines the distance in pixels between the top edge of the browser window and the content (e.g., `<BODY topmargin="150px">`).

title.en: BODY Hyperlink States: link, alink, and vlink
title.hi: हाइपरलिंक स्थितियां: link, alink और vlink

theory.en: The `<body>` tag configures visual feedback for hyperlinks across three interactive states: 1. `link` defines the color of unvisited links (default is blue); 2. `alink` (active link) defines the color of a link at the precise moment it is clicked (default is red); 3. `vlink` (visited link) defines the color of a link that has already been visited by the user (default is purple). E.g., `<BODY link="green" alink="pink" vlink="red">`.
theory.hi: BODY टैग हाइपरलिंक की तीन अवस्थाओं के रंग तय करता है: 1. `link`—अनविज़िटेड (unvisited) लिंक का रंग तय करता है (डिफ़ॉल्ट: नीला); 2. `alink` (Active link)—क्लिक करते समय सक्रिय लिंक का रंग तय करता है (डिफ़ॉल्ट: लाल); 3. `vlink` (Visited link)—पहले से विज़िट किए जा चुके लिंक का रंग तय करता है (डिफ़ॉल्ट: बैंगनी/purple)।

title.en: The FONT Tag: face, color, and size

theory.en: The `<FONT>...</FONT>` tag is a container tag used to alter the visual appearance of text within a web page. It features three primary attributes: `face` specifies the typeface family name (e.g., `<FONT face="broadway">`); `color` defines the text color (e.g., `<FONT color="green">`); and `size` sets the font size scale (e.g., `<FONT size="18">`).

title.en: HTML Comments: Purpose and Syntax
title.hi: HTML कमेन्ट: उपयोग और सिंटैक्स

theory.en: The HTML comment tag `<!-- ... -->` is an empty, unrendered tag used to insert developer notes and documentation into source code. Any text, tags, or code placed between `<!--` and `-->` are completely ignored by the web browser and not displayed on the web page. Comments help explain code logic and can temporarily disable code segments during testing.

theory.en: Hyperlinks connect web resources across the Internet using the anchor tag `...`. When hovering over a link, the mouse pointer turns into a hand icon. HTML supports two types of linking: 1. External Linking opens external websites or documents using `href` (e.g., `Open Gmail`); 2. Internal Linking jumps to another section of the same page by pairing a named anchor `` with a target link ``.

title.en: HTML Tables: table, tr, th, and td

theory.en:
In HTML, structured data tables are constructed using the `...
` container tag. Rows are created using `...` (Table Row). Within each row, column header cells are defined with `...` (Table Heading, bold and centered by default), and standard data cells are defined with `...` (Table Data). Table formatting attributes include `border` (border width), `bgcolor` (background color), and `align` (table or row alignment).
